title: Homily III — The tomb finer than Eden and the ark

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily III on the Dormition, cols. 753-757 (PDF leaves 418-420)

source_text:
Σήμερον ἡ νοητὴ κλίμαξ ἡ ἔμψυχος, δι' ἧς καταβὰς ὁ Ὕψιστος ἐπὶ γῆς ὤφθη, καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη, τῷ θανάτῳ χρησαμένη κλίματι γῆθεν εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀνεφοίτησεν. Σήμερον ἡ ἐπίγειος τράπεζα, ἡ τὸν οὐράνιον τῆς ζωῆς ἄρτον τὸν τῆς θεότητος ἄνθρακα ἀπειρογάμως βαστάσασα, ἀπὸ γῆς ἤρθη πρὸς οὐρανούς, καὶ τῇ κατ' ἀνατολὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ πύλῃ, πύλαι οὐρανοῦ ἐπήρθησαν. Σήμερον ἐκ τῆς ἐπιγείου Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἡ πόλις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ ἔμψυχος πρὸς τὴν ἄνω Ἱερουσαλὴμ μετατίθεται, καὶ τὸν πρωτότοκον πάσης κτίσεως, τὸν ἐκ Πατρὸς μονογενῆ, πρωτότοκον ἐξ αὐτῆς μονογενῆ κυήσασα, ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶν πρωτοτόκων αὐλίζεται, καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς Κυρίου ἡ ἔμψυχός τε καὶ λογικὴ πρὸς τὴν τοῦ Υἱοῦ ἀνάπαυσιν μετανίσταται. Πύλαι παραδείσου ἀνοίγονται, καὶ τὴν θεοφόρον ὑποδέχονται ἄρουραν, ἐξ ἧς τὸ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς ξύλον βλαστῆσαν τὴν παρακοὴν τῆς Εὔας καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τοῦ Ἀδὰμ διαλέλυκε.

Χριστὸς οὗτος, ὁ τῆς ζωῆς τῶν ἁπάντων αἴτιος, ἄντρον λελαξευμένον, ὄρος τὸ ἀλατόμητον ὑποδέχεται, ἐξ οὗ λίθος χειρῶν ἄνευ τμηθεὶς τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐπλήρωσεν· ἡ παστὰς τῆς θείας τοῦ Λόγου σαρκώσεως, ὡς ἐν θαλάμῳ τῷ πανευκλεεῖ ἀναπέπαυται τάφῳ, ὅθεν πρὸς τὸν οὐράνιον ἄνεισι νυμφῶνα, τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ Θεῷ ἀριδήλως συμβασιλεύουσα, καὶ τὸν τάφον παστάδα τοῖς ἐπὶ γῆς καταλέλοιπεν.

Παστάδα τὸν τάφον; Ναὶ παστάδος πάσης παναγλαέστερον, οὐ χρυσοῦ περιλάμψεσιν, οὐκ ἀργύρου φανότητι, καὶ λίθων διαυγείαις ἀστράπτουσαν, καὶ σειρῶν νήμασι, καὶ χρυσονήστῳ ἐσθῆτι, καὶ ἁλουργίδι κεκλωσμένη, ἀλλὰ θεοφεγγεῖ αἴγλῃ τοῦ παναγίου Πνεύματος· οὐ σωμάτων συνάφειαν τοῖς γῆς ἐρασταῖς, τοῖς δὲ δεσμίοις τοῦ Πνεύματος ψυχῶν ὁσίων ζωὴν προξενοῦσαν, πρὸς Θεὸν πάσης ἀμείνω καὶ γλυκυτέραν κατάστασιν.

Οὗτος ὁ τάφος τῆς Ἐδὲμ ὡραιότερος· καὶ ἵνα μὴ λέγω τὴν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τοῦ δυσμενοῦς εὔνοιαν, τὴν χρηστήν, ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω, συμβουλήν, τὸν φθόνον, τὴν ἀπάτην, τῆς Εὔας τὴν μαλακότητα, τὴν πιθανότητα, τὸ γλυκὺ καὶ πικρὸν δέλεαρ, δι' ἧς ἐκλάπη τὸν νοῦν, καὶ τὸν ὁμόζυγα κέκλοφε, τὴν παρακοήν, τὴν ἐξορίαν, τὸν θάνατον, ἵνα μὴ ταῦτα λέγων τὴν ἑορτὴν ἐκτελῶ κατηφείας ὑπόθεσιν· οὗτος ἀπὸ γῆς σῶμα θνητὸν εἰς οὐρανὸν μετεώρισεν· ἐκείνη δὲ ὑψόθεν εἰς γῆν τὸν γενάρχην κατήγαγεν. Ἢ γὰρ οὐκ ἐν αὐτῇ· Γῆ εἶ, καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ, ὁ κατ' εἰκόνα θείαν γεγονὼς κατακέκριται;

Οὗτος ὁ τάφος τῆς πάλαι σκηνῆς τιμιώτερος, τὴν λογικήν τε καὶ ἔμψυχον, θεοφεγγῆ λυχνίαν δεξάμενος, καὶ τὴν ζωηφόρον τράπεζαν, οὐ καρποὺς προθέσεως, ἀλλ' οὐράνιον, οὐ πῦρ ὑλικόν, ἀλλ' ἄϋλον δεξαμένην πῦρ τῆς θεότητος. Οὗτος ὁ τάφος τῆς Μωσαϊκῆς κιβωτοῦ ὀλβιώτερος, εὐμοιρήσας οὐ σκιὰς καὶ τύπους, ἀλλ' αὐτὴν τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Ἐδείξατο γὰρ τὴν ἀκίβδηλον καὶ χρυσοειδῆ στάμνον, τὴν τὸ οὐράνιον μάννα καρποφορήσασαν, πλάκα ἔμψυχον, Λόγον Θεοῦ δακτύλῳ τῷ παναλκεστάτῳ Πνεύματι δεξαμένην σαρκωθησόμενον, Λόγον τὸν ἐνυπόστατον, τὸ χρυσοῦν θυμιατήριον, τὴν τὸν θεῖον κυήσασα ἄνθρακα, καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν κτίσιν εὐωδιάσασαν.
pass_a_gloss: [0] Today (σήμερον) the intelligible/spiritual (νοητή) ladder (κλίμαξ), the ensouled/living (ἔμψυχος) one, through which having come down (καταβάς) the Most High (Ὕψιστος) on earth was seen (ὤφθη) and with men lived-together, having used death (θάνατος) as a ladder from earth to heavens went up. Today the earthly (ἐπίγειος) table (τράπεζα), the one having carried (βαστάσασα) without-marriage the heavenly bread (ἄρτος) of life (ζωή), the coal (ἄνθραξ) of the Godhead (θεότης), from earth was lifted (ἤρθη) to heavens; and for the gate (πύλη) of God toward the east, gates of heaven were lifted up (ἐπήρθησαν). Today from the earthly Jerusalem the city (πόλις) of God, the living one, to the Jerusalem above (ἄνω) is transferred; and having conceived/borne (κυήσασα) the firstborn of all creation (κτίσις), the only-begotten (μονογενής) from the Father, as firstborn from herself, only-begotten, in the Church (Ἐκκλησία) of the firstborn she lodges (αὐλίζεται); and the ark (κιβωτός) of the Lord, the living and rational (λογική) one, to the rest (ἀνάπαυσις) of the Son moves over. Gates of paradise are opened and receive the God-bearing (θεοφόρος) field (ἄρουρα), from which the tree (ξύλον) of eternal life having sprouted (βλαστῆσαν) the disobedience (παρακοή) of Eve and the deadness (νέκρωσις) of Adam has undone (διαλέλυκε). [1] Christ (is) this one, the cause (αἴτιος) of the life of all; a hewn cave (ἄντρον) the unquarried mountain (ὄρος) receives, from which a stone (λίθος) without hands cut (τμηθείς) filled (ἐπλήρωσεν) the inhabited world (οἰκουμένη); the bridal chamber (παστάς) of the divine incarnation (σάρκωσις) of the Word (Λόγος) as in a chamber (θάλαμος) has come to rest in the all-glorious tomb (τάφος), whence to the heavenly bridal hall (νυμφών) she goes up (ἄνεισι), with the Son and God clearly/conspicuously (ἀριδήλως) co-reigning, and the tomb as bridal chamber to those on earth she has left behind. [2] Bridal chamber the tomb? Yes, than every bridal chamber more all-splendid, not with gleamings of gold, not with brightness (φανότης) of silver and clearnesses (διαυγείαι) of stones flashing, and with threads (νήματα) of cords, and gold-spun garment (ἐσθής), and purple (ἁλουργίς) woven, but with God-lit (θεοφεγγής) radiance (αἴγλη) of the all-holy Spirit (Πνεῦμα); not union (συνάφεια) of bodies for the lovers (ἐρασταί) of earth, but for the prisoners (δέσμιοι) of the Spirit procuring life of holy (ὅσιαι) souls, a state toward God better than all and sweeter. [3] This tomb than Eden more beautiful; and so that I do not speak of the goodwill (εὔνοια) of the enemy (δυσμενής) in it, the kindly (χρηστή), so to speak, counsel (συμβουλή), the envy (φθόνος), the deceit (ἀπάτη), the softness/weakness (μαλακότης) of Eve, the persuasion/credulity (πιθανότης), the sweet and bitter bait (δέλεαρ), through which (δι' ἧς) she was robbed (ἐκλάπη) as to the mind (νοῦς) and her yoke-mate (ὁμόζυγος) she has robbed (κέκλοφε), the disobedience, the exile (ἐξορία), the death, so that saying these things I do not make the feast (ἑορτή) a subject (ὑπόθεσις) of gloom (κατήφεια); this (tomb) from earth a mortal (θνητόν) body raised up into heaven; but that one from on high to earth the founder of the race (γενάρχης) brought down (κατήγαγεν). For (is it) not in it (that) 'Earth you are, and into earth you shall depart' (ἀπελεύσῃ) the one having come to be according to the divine image (εἰκών) has been condemned? [4] This tomb than the tent (σκηνή) of old more precious, having received the rational and living, God-lit lampstand (λυχνία), and the life-bearing (ζωηφόρος) table, (having received) not fruits of setting-forth (πρόθεσις) but heavenly (bread), not material (ὑλικόν) fire (πῦρ) but having received immaterial (ἄϋλον) fire of the Godhead. This tomb than the Mosaic ark more blessed, having had as lot not shadows (σκιαί) and types (τύποι) but the truth (ἀλήθεια) itself. For it showed/received the unadulterated (ἀκίβδηλος) and gold-like jar (στάμνος), the one having borne as fruit the heavenly manna (μάννα), a living tablet (πλάξ), having received by finger (δάκτυλος) the all-mightiest Spirit the Word of God about to be incarnated, the Word the enhypostatic, the golden censer, the one (τήν) having conceived the divine coal and having made all creation fragrant.

pass_b_english: Today the spiritual and living ladder (Genesis 28:12), by which the Most High came down and was seen on earth and lived among men (Baruch 3:37), has used death as a ladder and gone up from earth to heaven. Today the earthly table, which without knowing marriage carried the heavenly bread of life (John 6:35), the coal of the Godhead, has been lifted from earth to heaven; and for the eastern gate of God (Ezekiel 44:1–2) the gates of heaven have been lifted up (Psalm 24:7). Today the living city of God is moved from the earthly Jerusalem to the Jerusalem above (Galatians 4:26). She who bore as her firstborn and only son the firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15), the Only-begotten of the Father, now dwells in the church of the firstborn (Hebrews 12:23); and the ark of the Lord, living and endowed with reason, passes over to the rest of her Son (Psalm 132:8). The gates of paradise are opened and receive the field that bore God, from which sprang the tree of eternal life that undid the disobedience of Eve and the death of Adam.

This tree is Christ, the cause of life for all. A hewn cave receives the mountain no hand had quarried, from which a stone cut without hands has filled the whole world (Daniel 2:34–35). The bridal chamber of the divine incarnation of the Word rests in the all-glorious tomb as in a chamber. From there she goes up to the heavenly bridal hall, reigning in full view with her Son and God; and she has left the tomb behind as a bridal chamber for those on earth.

The tomb a bridal chamber? Yes, more splendid than any bridal chamber: not flashing with the gleam of gold, the brightness of silver and the clear sparkle of precious stones, not woven of silken threads, of robes spun with gold and of purple, but with the radiance of the all-holy Spirit, bright with the light of God. It does not bring about the joining of bodies for those who love the earth; for those who are prisoners of the Spirit it brings about the life of holy souls, a state with God better and sweeter than any other.

This tomb is lovelier than Eden. I will not speak of what happened there: the goodwill of the enemy, his kindly advice, if I may call it that, the envy, the deceit, the weakness of Eve, the persuasion, the sweet and bitter bait, through which her mind was stolen and she in turn stole away her husband, the disobedience, the exile, the death. I will not speak of these, so as not to make the feast an occasion of gloom. This tomb raised a mortal body from earth to heaven; Eden brought the father of our race down from on high to earth. For was it not in Eden that he who had been made in the divine image (Genesis 1:27) was condemned with the words, “You are earth, and to earth you shall return” (Genesis 3:19)?

This tomb is more precious than the tabernacle of old (Hebrews 9:2). It has received the living lampstand, endowed with reason and shining with the light of God, and the life-bearing table, which held not the bread of the presence but heavenly bread, and received not material fire but the immaterial fire of the Godhead. This tomb is more blessed than the ark of Moses, for its portion was not shadows and figures but the truth itself. For it received the pure and golden jar that bore the heavenly manna as its fruit (Hebrews 9:4); the living tablet which, by the finger that is the all-powerful Spirit (Exodus 31:18), received the Word of God who was to become flesh, the Word who subsists in his own person; the golden censer, she who conceived the divine coal and filled all creation with fragrance.

choices.note: Doubtful readings, all from the source row's notes and checked against the facing Latin of Migne (col. 755-758): printed κλίματι rendered as κλίμακι, 'ladder' (Latin 'per scalam').

'Χριστὸς οὗτος, ὁ τῆς ζωῆς τῶν ἁπάντων αἴτιος' opens the editorial second paragraph but belongs with the tree of life at the end of the first: the Latin reads it as apposition to the tree ('Christus nimirum'); the English says 'This tree is Christ, the cause of life for all', which supplies 'tree' to carry οὗτος across the break.
Printed κεκλωσμένη and κυήσασα treated as κεκλωσμένην and κυήσασαν (grammar requires agreement; sense unchanged).
σειρῶν νήμασι ('threads of cords') rendered 'silken threads' with the Latin 'sericis', which read σηρῶν; possible minor variance.
Printed καρποὺς προθέσεως rendered 'the bread of the presence' (the usual phrase is ἄρτους προθέσεως;
Latin 'panem propositionis'); literal 'fruits of the setting-forth'.
Printed Ἐδείξατο ('displayed') rendered 'received' with the Latin 'Recepit' and the parallel δεξάμενος earlier in the paragraph; if Ἐδείξατο stands, read 'it displayed'.
Migne's note (67): Sangerm.
ὑψωθεῖσα for ὑψόθεν (Eden 'exalted' brought him down);
English follows the print.
Πρωτότοκον ἐξ αὐτῆς μονογενῆ rendered 'as her firstborn and only son'.
ἔμψυχος rendered 'living' throughout;
λογική 'endowed with reason'.
Scripture: Baruch is cited in English numbering (Baruch 3:37 in KJV/RSV/NRSV);
Migne's margin gives Baruch III, 38 (LXX/Vulgate numbering).
Genesis 3:19 is in the margin.
Psalm 24:7 = LXX/Vulgate Psalm 23:7 (ἐπάρθητε, πύλαι).
Psalm 132:8 = LXX/Vulgate Psalm 131:8 (the ark and the Lord's rest).
Genesis 28:12 cited for Jacob's ladder;
Ezekiel 44:1-2 for the shut eastern gate;
Daniel 2:34-35 for the stone cut without hands that filled the earth;
Hebrews 9:2 and 9:4 for the furnishings of the tabernacle and the ark (lampstand, table, golden censer, golden jar of manna, tablets);
Exodus 31:18 for the tablets written by the finger of God; the finger as the Spirit reflects Luke 11:20 / Matthew 12:28 (not cited).

Left uncited as possible only: Isaiah 6:6 (the coal), Genesis 2:9 (tree of life), Psalm 87:3 (city of God, cited in 1.1), Psalm 19:5 (bridegroom's chamber), Luke 2:7 (firstborn), Hebrews 10:1 (shadow), Exodus 16:33 (jar of manna).
Reviewer: δακτύλῳ τῷ παναλκεστάτῳ Πνεύματι is an apposition (the finger is the Spirit), rendered 'by the finger that is the all-powerful Spirit' so the Spirit is not read as the object received;
Θεοῦ is taken with Λόγον ('the Word of God').
δι' ἧς (feminine) cannot refer to the neuter δέλεαρ alone; the English 'through which' after the series covers the persuasion and the bait.
Ἐδείξατο confirmed as printed on the page image (leaf 419).

source_notes: Witness: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), sources/pg-96.pdf (sha256 5797ee4d...6e765bea), col. 753 foot (PDF leaf 418, left; opening words 'Σήμερον ἡ νοητὴ κλίμαξ ... τοῖς ἀνθρώ-'), all of col. 756 (PDF leaf 419, right column), and the first three lines of col. 757 (PDF leaf 420, left, ending 'εὐωδιάσασαν.'). Variant in Migne's note: ὑψόθεν — (67) Sangerm. ὑψωθεῖσα. Scripture margin at foot of col. 756: Baruch III, 38 ('appeared on earth and lived among men', at 'ἐπὶ γῆς ὤφθη, καὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις συνανεστράφη'); Gen. III, 19 (the italic 'Γῆ εἶ, καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ'). Doubtful readings, all transcribed as printed and checked at 600 dpi: 'κλίματι' (κλίμακι, 'ladder', expected from the image of the ladder); 'Χριστὸς οὗτος' is clearly printed though the construction is awkward; 'κεκλωσμένη' (κεκλωσμένην expected, agreeing with παστάδα/ἀστράπτουσαν); 'καρποὺς προθέσεως' (where ἄρτους προθέσεως, showbread, would be the usual phrase); 'κυήσασα' at the top of col. 757 (κυήσασαν expected after τὴν); the opening particle of 'Ἢ γὰρ οὐκ ἐν αὐτῇ' has a faint mark and could be Ἦ. 'αἴγλῃ' and 'πύλῃ' show the iota subscript at 600 dpi. Transcribed by Claude from the page images (pdftoppm 300 dpi crops, doubtful spots re-read at 600 dpi), not from the scan OCR. Paragraph breaks inside the section are editorial; the print runs each numbered section as one paragraph. Migne's footnote markers (63)-(71) and Scripture margin numbers are left out of the Greek and reported here.
